title: Prelude in C major, BWV 846
composer: J. S. Bach (Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I)
global_summary: Bach's C-major Prelude (WTC I) is a 34-bar arpeggio study in which each bar projects a single harmony. Over a tonic statement, two tonicisations of the dominant, a chain of applied diminished sevenths, a structural dominant pedal (mm.24-30) and a closing tonic pedal, the piece traces a complete I -> V -> I tonal arch. The diatonic triads and sevenths are analysed in full; the nine chromatic bars (6, 10, 12, 14, 20, 22, 23, 27, 31 -- secondary dominants and applied diminished sevenths) are marked honestly as requiring the reserved chromatic layer. Pitch data verified against the music21 34-bar corpus edition (no Schwencke bar).

sections.label: Opening tonic statement
sections.description: I - ii7 - V7 - I: the tonic is established and prolonged.

sections.label: Tonal expansion
sections.description: Submediant colour and two V7/V tonicisations push toward the dominant.

sections.label: Sequential descent
sections.description: Applied diminished sevenths alternate with diatonic sevenths: ii - vii0 - I - IV - ii - V - I.

sections.label: Pre-dominant intensification
sections.description: V7/IV, IV and applied diminished sevenths intensify toward the structural dominant.

sections.label: Dominant pedal
sections.description: A sustained G pedal with cadential six-fours and an applied vii07/V -- the structural dominant.

sections.label: Tonic pedal and close
sections.description: C pedal, a last V7/IV colour, then the final perfect authentic cadence.

cadences.explanation: Opening authentic resolution (V6/5 - I) closing the first phrase.
Perfect authentic cadence closing the prelude: the long dominant prolongation (mm.24-33) resolves to the tonic C in m.34.

slices.explanation: Opening tonic: C major, arpeggiated (I).
Supertonic seventh (ii7, D-F-A-C) over the tonic bass -- predominant motion away from I.
Dominant seventh in first inversion (V6/5, G7 with B in the bass) -- pulls back to tonic.
Return to tonic (I) -- completes the opening I - ii7 - V7 - I phrase.
Submediant (vi, A minor) colouring the tonic region; sometimes read as I added-sixth.
Secondary dominant V7/V (D7, with chromatic F#) -- tonicises the dominant. Requires the reserved secondary-dominant layer: mapped to the D7 network node, not a diatonic C-major triad.
Dominant triad in first inversion (V6) -- the F# of m.6 resolves; we are firmly on the dominant.
Tonic with a major seventh (Imaj7, C-E-G-B); the B is a diatonic colour tone.
Submediant seventh (vi7, A-C-E-G) -- diatonic, prolongs the tonic region.
Secondary dominant V7/V (D7) again, now in root position. Chromatic F#; reserved secondary-dominant layer.
Dominant triad (V, G major) in root position.
Applied fully-diminished seventh vii07/ii (C#-E-G-Bb) leading to the supertonic. Chromatic C#/Bb; reserved diminished-seventh layer -- mapped to the C#-dim network node.
Supertonic in first inversion (ii6, D minor) -- predominant, the target of the previous applied chord.

Leading-tone fully-diminished seventh (vii07, B-D-F-Ab) -- dominant function resolving to tonic. The Ab is borrowed from C minor (chromatic); the underlying B-D-F is the diatonic vii°, so the Atlas lights that triad.
Tonic in first inversion (I6) -- the vii07 resolves to C.
Subdominant with a major seventh (IV7, F-A-C-E) -- diatonic predominant colour.
Supertonic seventh (ii7, D-F-A-C) in root position -- predominant.
Dominant seventh (V7, G-B-D-F) over a low G -- strong dominant.
Tonic (I) -- local resolution.

Secondary dominant V7/IV (C7, with chromatic Bb) -- turns the tonic into a dominant of the subdominant. Reserved secondary-dominant layer; mapped to the C7 network node, NOT the tonic triad (its triad merely coincides with I).
Subdominant (IV, F major) -- the C7 of m.20 resolves to F.
Applied fully-diminished seventh vii07/V (F#-A-C-Eb) intensifying toward the dominant. Chromatic F#/Eb; reserved diminished-seventh layer -- F#-dim network node.
Leading-tone diminished seventh (vii07, B-D-F-Ab) with passing C/D -- dominant preparation. Chromatic Ab (from C minor); the diatonic B-D-F triad is the vii°.
Dominant seventh (V7) -- start of the long dominant pedal on G (mm.24-30).
Cadential six-four (I6/4): a C-major triad sounding over the dominant G pedal -- it carries dominant tension despite being a tonic triad.
Dominant seventh (V7) over the G pedal -- the six-four leans onto the dominant.
Applied diminished seventh (vii07/V, F#-A-C-Eb) decorating the dominant pedal. Chromatic; reserved diminished-seventh layer.
Cadential six-four again (I6/4 over the G pedal).
A suspension stack over the dominant pedal (G-C-D-F, with no leading-tone B) -- not a single triad; reads as a dominant suspension. Marked ambiguous (no clean triad).
Dominant seventh (V7) -- the suspension resolves; the dominant is confirmed.
Secondary dominant V7/IV (C7) over the tonic pedal that begins here (mm.31-34). Chromatic Bb; reserved secondary-dominant layer.
Supertonic seventh (ii7) over the tonic C pedal -- predominant within the final tonic prolongation.
The penultimate dominant: a dense V7(13) figuration (G-B-D-F with added C/E) over the tonic pedal -- maximum dominant tension before the close.
Final tonic (I) -- the perfect authentic cadence resolves; the prelude ends on C major.
